Load the tidyverse

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Data

For this assignment, we will use data from a study on elephants and the effects of poaching on tusk size.

Reference: Chiyo, Patrick I., Vincent Obanda, and David K. Korir. “Illegal tusk harvest and the decline of tusk size in the African elephant.” Ecology and Evolution 5, 22: 5216–5229 (2015). Data deposited at Dryad Digital Repository.

1. Before starting data analysis, read the abstract of the paper to get an idea of the questions being asked. In 2-3 sentences, describe what the study is testing and the variables involved.
  #This study is looking at if ivory poaching has caused elephants to develop smaller tusks over a period of time, in order for this to be tested tusk sizes were compared between elephants before poaching and after.




2. Load elephants.csv and store it as a new object called elephants.

5. Use mutate() Change the variables years_of_sample_collection, elephant_id, and sex to factors. Be sure to store the output as a new dataframe and use it for the remaining questions.

elephants <- elephants %>%
  mutate(
    years_of_sample_collection = as.factor(years_of_sample_collection), 
    elephant_id= as.factor(elephant_id),
    sex = as.factor(sex)
  )




6. From which years were data collected? Show the sample periods below.

levels(elephants$years_of_sample_collection)
## [1] "1966-68" "2005-13"




7. How many males and females were sampled in this study?

elephants %>%
  count(sex)
## # A tibble: 2 × 2
##   sex       n
##   <fct> <int>
## 1 f       416
## 2 m       361




8. What is the mean, median, and standard deviation for age of males and females included in the study? Separate the results by year of sample collection. Does the sampling look even between years and sexes?

elephants %>%
  group_by(years_of_sample_collection, sex) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_age= mean(estimated_age_years, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_age = median(estimated_age_years, na.rm= TRUE),
    sd_age = sd(estimated_age_years, na.rm = TRUE),
    total= n()
  )
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'years_of_sample_collection'. You can
## override using the `.groups` argument.
## # A tibble: 4 × 6
## # Groups:   years_of_sample_collection [2]
##   years_of_sample_collection sex   mean_age median_age sd_age total
##   <fct>                      <fct>    <dbl>      <dbl>  <dbl> <int>
## 1 1966-68                    f         17.6       15    13.6    323
## 2 1966-68                    m         10.8        8     9.19   282
## 3 2005-13                    f         17.9       17.5  11.0     93
## 4 2005-13                    m         16.7        9    13.9     79




9. Is age (independent variable) a positive predictor of tusk length (dependent variable)? Create a plot that shows the relationship between these variables and add a linear model fit line.

elephants %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=estimated_age_years, y= tusk_length_in_cm)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method= lm, se= TRUE) + 
  labs(x= "Age(years)", y= "Tusk length (cm)", title= "Relationship between tusk length and Age in Elephants")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 182 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 182 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

11. The authors argue that because poachers preferentially target elephants with large tusks, this has resulted in a decrease in average tusk length. Is this supported by the data? Show your code and calculations below.

elephants %>%
  group_by(years_of_sample_collection) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_tusk = mean (tusk_length_in_cm, na.rm = TRUE), 
    sd_tusk= sd(tusk_length_in_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  )
## # A tibble: 2 × 4
##   years_of_sample_collection mean_tusk sd_tusk     n
##   <fct>                          <dbl>   <dbl> <int>
## 1 1966-68                         96.9    39.1   605
## 2 2005-13                         77.2    33.9   172
elephants %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= years_of_sample_collection, y= tusk_length_in_cm)) + 
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(
    title= "Tusk Length in cm across different periods",
    x= "Period of Time", 
    y= "Tusk Length in cm"
  )
## Warning: Removed 180 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).




12. Male elephants reach effective sexual maturity at 25 years while females are sexually mature at 12 years. Make a new dataframe that extracts only the males and females at sexual maturity. Then, make a plot that shows the range of tusk length between the two sample periods for these mature elephants.


matured_elephants <- elephants %>%
  filter(
    (sex == "m" & estimated_age_years >= 25) |
    (sex == "f" & estimated_age_years >= 12)
  )

ggplot(data= matured_elephants, aes(x= years_of_sample_collection, y= tusk_length_in_cm)) + 
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(title = "Tusk length in cm across different period in matured elephants", x= "Period of time", y= "Tusk Length")
## Warning: Removed 44 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).
